questions.q: To what does Qoheleth compare the consequences of a little foolishness?
questions.a: Qoheleth compares the consequences of a little foolishness to a few flies in perfumer’s oil that cause it to stink.

questions.q: What does the heart of a wise person do compared to the heart of a fool?
questions.a: The heart of a wise person goes toward the good, but the heart of a fool goes toward evil.

questions.q: What proves to everyone that a man is a fool?
questions.a: When a man’s behavior lacks good sense, this proves to everyone that he is a fool.

questions.q: What does Qoheleth say a person should do if the ruler becomes angry with him?
questions.a: He should not leave his responsibilities, because remaining calm will lessen the ruler’s anger and cause great sins to leave.

questions.q: What misfortune does Qoheleth say he saw under the sun?
questions.a: He saw a misfortune that is like an unintentional sin that comes from the authority.

questions.q: Who is placed in many high places, and who sits in the lowly place?
questions.a: Folly is placed in many high places, and rich people sit in the lowly place.

questions.q: What did Qoheleth see slaves doing?
questions.a: Qoheleth saw slaves riding on horses like princes and saw princes walking like slaves do.

questions.q: What can happen to someone who digs a pit?
questions.a: If someone digs a pit, he might fall into the it.

questions.q: What can happen to someone who pulls up stones or splits wood?
questions.a: Someone who pulls up stones or who splits wood can become injured.

questions.q: What must a man do if he does not sharpen a dull iron blade?
questions.a: If a man does not sharpen a dull iron blade, he must use more strength.

questions.q: What is of no benefit to the snake charmer?
questions.a: If a snake bites before it is charmed, the snake charmer gets no benefit.

questions.q: What is a difference between the words of a wise person and the words of a foolish person?
questions.a: The words of a wise person bring honor to him, but the words of a foolish person will bring harm to him.

questions.q: What are the beginning and the end of a fool’s words?
questions.a: The beginning of a fool’s words is foolishness, and the end is evil insanity.

questions.q: What does Qoheleth say a person does not know?
questions.a: A person does not know what might happen either tomorrow or in the future.

questions.q: What happens to foolish people because of their toil?
questions.a: Their toil wearies them, so that they do not know how to find their way into their own city.

questions.q: When is there trouble for the land?
questions.a: There is trouble for the land if its king is a youth and its princes indulge themselves instead of attending to their responsibilities.

questions.q: When is the land blessed?
questions.a: The land is blessed when its king is a son of nobles and its princes eat at the proper time, with strength and not with drunkenness.

questions.q: What happens to the house because of laziness and idle hands?
questions.a: Because of laziness the beams of the roof sink, and because of idle hands the house leaks.

questions.q: What does silver do, according to Qoheleth?
questions.a: Silver is useful for responding to life’s problems.

questions.q: Why should people not belittle a king or a rich person, even in private?
questions.a: What you say might be repeated in public as if it was carried by a bird.

commentary.text: To preserve a character for wisdom. (Eccl. 10:1-3) Respecting subjects and rulers. (Eccl. 10:4-10) Of foolish talk. (Eccl. 10:11-15) Duties of rulers and subjects. (Eccl. 10:16-20)

Eccl. 10:1-3 Those especially who make a profession of religion, should keep from all appearances of evil. A wise man has great advantage over a fool, who is always at a loss when he has anything to do. Sin is the reproach of sinners, wherever they go, and shows their folly.

Eccl. 10:4-10 Solomon appears to caution men not to seek redress in a hasty manner, nor to yield to pride and revenge. Do not, in a passion, quit thy post of duty; wait awhile, and thou wilt find that yielding pacifies great offences. Men are not preferred according to their merit. And those are often most forward to offer help, who are least aware of the difficulties, or the consequences. The same remark is applied to the church, or the body of Christ, that all the members should have the same care one for another.

Eccl. 10:11-15 There is a practice in the East, of charming serpents by music. The babbler's tongue is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison; and contradiction only makes it the more violent. We must find the way to keep him gentle. But by rash, unprincipled, or slanderous talk, he brings open or secret vengeance upon himself. Would we duly consider our own ignorance as to future events, it would cut off many idle words which we foolishly multiply. Fools toil a great deal to no purpose. They do not understand the plainest things, such as the entrance into a great city. But it is the excellency of the way to the heavenly city, that it is a high-way, in which the simplest wayfaring men shall not err, Is. 25:8. But sinful folly makes men miss that only way to happiness.

Eccl. 10:16-20 The happiness of a land depends on the character of its rulers. The people cannot be happy when their princes are childish, and lovers of pleasure. Slothfulness is of ill consequence both to private and public affairs. Money, of itself, will neither feed nor clothe, though it answers the occasions of this present life, as what is to be had, may generally be had for money. But the soul, as it is not redeemed, so it is not maintained with corruptible things, as silver and gold. God sees what men do, and hears what they say in secret; and, when he pleases, brings it to light by strange and unsuspected ways. If there be hazard in secret thoughts and whispers against earthly rulers, what must be the peril from every deed, word, or thought of rebellion against the King of kings, and Lord of lords! He seeth in secret. His ear is ever open. Sinner! curse not THIS KING in thy inmost thought. Your curses cannot affect Him; but his curse, coming down upon you, will sink you to the lowest hell.
